title: Multimodal Large Language Models

children.title: Foundations: Multimodal Pretraining, Architectures, and Representation Learning
Representation Learning: Grounding, Alignment, and Cross-Modal Semantics
children.rationale: These papers focus on the theoretical and empirical question of what multimodal pretraining actually learns—whether it grounds language, how cross-modal representations are structured, and the evolution of multimodal representation techniques.

children.title: Pretraining Architectures and Objectives: Vision-Language and Omni-Modal Models
children.rationale: These papers survey or introduce specific pretraining architectures, objectives, and datasets—from dual-encoder and encoder-decoder VLP models to tri-modal (vision-audio-language) systems—covering the design space of how multimodal pretraining is operationalized.

children.title: Scaling to General-Purpose Multimodal Foundation Models and LLM Architectures
children.rationale: These papers address the transition from task-specific pretrained models to large-scale, general-purpose multimodal systems—including jointly-scaled vision-language models (PaLI), surveys of the full multimodal foundation model landscape, LLM architectural trends, and instruction-tuned multimodal LLMs.

These papers establish the core pretraining paradigms, model architectures (ViT, encoder-decoder, joint vision-language models), and representation learning methods that underpin all downstream MLLMs.

children.title: Instruction Tuning, Efficient Adaptation, and Model Development
Instruction-Tuning Data Construction and Core Visual LLM Architectures
Instruction-Tuning Data Construction: Generation, Scaling, and Quality
children.rationale: These papers all address the problem of how to create, scale, and improve the quality of multimodal instruction-tuning data, from the original LLaVA GPT-4-based generation approach to SVIT's large-scale expansion and VIGC's iterative generation-and-correction paradigm.

children.title: Core Visual LLM Architectures: Cross-Modal Alignment and Structural Design
children.rationale: These papers focus on architectural choices for multimodal LLMs—from tutorial-level overviews of building multimodal GPT-4-like models, to region-level encoder integration for fine-grained alignment (PVIT), to frozen-LLM inner-adaptor designs that preserve NLP capabilities (IAA).

These papers establish the foundational paradigm of visual instruction tuning—generating instruction-following data and training end-to-end multimodal models—including LLaVA, SVIT, VIGC, PVIT, and the CVPR tutorial overview.

children.title: Efficient Adaptation, Lightweight Architectures, and Knowledge Distillation
children.rationale: These papers address the challenge of reducing computational cost and preserving language capabilities through parameter-efficient adapters, frozen LLM strategies, and knowledge distillation from large to small MLLMs.

children.title: Domain-Specific and Task-Specific Instruction Tuning Applications
children.rationale: These papers apply instruction tuning to specialized domains and tasks—text-rich image reading, semiconductor microscopy, domain-specific visual multitasks, and mutual reinforcement of perception and comprehension.

children.title: Surveys, Benchmarks, and Broad Overviews of MLLMs
children.rationale: These papers provide comprehensive surveys of MLLM architectures and training strategies, and systematic benchmark reviews for evaluating multimodal capabilities across diverse tasks.
These papers focus on building capable MLLMs through visual instruction tuning, data generation, parameter-efficient adapters, knowledge distillation, and domain-specific fine-tuning strategies.

children.title: Evaluation, Benchmarking, Interpretability, and In-Context Learning
Evaluation and Benchmarking of Multimodal Large Language Models
children.rationale: These papers all construct or analyze benchmarks and evaluation frameworks to measure MLLM performance across multimodal tasks such as VQA, captioning, and reasoning.

children.title: Interpretability and In-Context Learning in Multimodal Large Language Models
children.rationale: These papers focus on understanding the internal mechanisms of MLLMs (attention visualization, explainability) and probing the emergent in-context learning capabilities of vision-language models.

These papers assess MLLM capabilities through comprehensive benchmarks, VQA-focused evaluations, multimodal in-context learning probes, and interpretability/explainability tools that reveal what models have learned.

rationale: The corpus naturally partitions into papers about foundational architectures and pretraining methods, papers about instruction tuning and efficient adaptation, and papers about evaluation/benchmarking and interpretability—moving from building blocks to deployment and assessment.
